cases.title: CDCHECKIGNORE with the switch off says so in one line and changes nothing
cases.expected: With the switch off, typing CDCHECKIGNORE prints 'Ignoring a finding is switched off in CE Settings. Nothing was changed.' at once, asks no question, and leaves no window or prompt behind; the four settings files are unchanged.
cases.why_not_unit: The refusal depends on the switch value CE read from Tim's real settings file when AutoCAD started, and on the real command line showing the one line with no question after it.
not_automated: The 'Command outcome' word for this refusal is recorded, not judged: BUG-862 says it is logged 'completed' and should say 'refused'. BUG-863 (the project record being saved on the off path) is not checked here.
The switch is read from Tim's file as it is (off). The ON paths of CDCHECKIGNORE (spec C17 to C19) need a settings profile and are not in this case.

cases.title: REDO still works after U and a mouse pick of a pit, five times in a row
cases.expected: First a control with no pick (draw a line, U, REDO: 'Everything has been redone'). Then five times: draw a line, U, click the pit P3 (handle 109D56) with the real mouse, wait 12 seconds, REDO: the command line says 'Everything has been redone' every time, never 'Nothing to redo'.
cases.why_not_unit: Whether REDO survives depends on what CE does in the seconds after a pick (the Inspector refresh) inside a real AutoCAD undo stack.
not_automated: The right-click CE menu half of BUG-861 and BUG-416 (the right-click menu is not read yet), and a second open drawing. This case is the one-drawing, real-mouse-pick version.

A pick made by the driver's typed LISP (v2 pick-first) is NOT used: in the probe run of 23 Oct 2026 (build 3.0.72) REDO answered 'Nothing to redo' after such a pick while the no-pick control worked, so that route cannot tell a CE fault from the typed LISP line itself.
